events.title: Cox Farms Fall Festival
events.venue: Cox Farms (15621 Braddock Rd)
events.why: Northern Virginia's classic fall festival with hayrides, farm animals, giant slides and cider doughnuts through its closing weekend.

events.title: 28th Bethesda Row Arts Festival
events.time: Sat 11 a.m.–6 p.m.; Sun 10 a.m.–5 p.m.
events.venue: Bethesda Row (Bethesda Ave, Elm St & Woodmont Ave)
events.why: One of the region's top juried outdoor art shows, with 180-plus artists along walkable streets lined with restaurants.

events.title: Howard University Homecoming: WHUT FamFest & International Yardfest
events.time: FamFest 11 a.m.–3 p.m.; Yardfest all afternoon
events.venue: Howard University, The Yard (2400 6th St NW)
events.why: A landmark HBCU homecoming pairing a kid-friendly family festival with a big afternoon of live music on the Yard.

events.title: Kingman Island Friends & Family Day
events.venue: Kingman & Heritage Islands Park (575 Oklahoma Ave NE)
events.why: A relaxed river-island festival with guided nature and bird walks, acoustic music and picnicking on flat, stroller-friendly trails.

events.title: PeopleCon 3: A Designed in the DMV Game Market
events.venue: People's Book (7014-A Westmoreland Ave)
events.why: An indie tabletop game market showcasing local designers and zines, plus an afternoon talk on games and Supreme Court history.

events.title: Shipgarten Oktoberfest Renaissance Festival
events.venue: Shipgarten (7581 Colshire Dr)
events.price: Free admission; food and drink extra
events.why: An outdoor beer garden festival with medieval flair, costumed characters, lawn games and food tents on dog-friendly turf.

events.title: Ward 4 Family Fun Day
events.venue: Riggs LaSalle Recreation Center (501 Riggs Rd NE)
events.why: A free city-hosted neighborhood day with games, music and giveaways at a local rec center.

events.title: Brookland Arts Walk Open Studios
events.venue: Brookland Arts Walk, Monroe Street Market (716 Monroe St NE)
events.why: A Saturday stroll through 27 working artist studios selling ceramics and prints along a car-free promenade.

events.title: Fall Harvest Family Days at George Washington's Mount Vernon
events.venue: George Washington's Mount Vernon (3200 Mount Vernon Memorial Hwy)
events.price: Included with admission ($28 adults; under 5 free)
events.why: Colonial harvest demonstrations, a straw bale maze and wagon rides on the estate's lawns above the Potomac.

events.title: The Great Baltimore Lantern Parade & Día de los Muertos Festival
events.time: Festival 4 p.m.; parade at dusk (about 7 p.m.)
events.venue: Patterson Park (2601 E Baltimore St)
events.why: Thousands of handmade glowing lanterns, giant puppets and marching bands wind through Patterson Park in Baltimore's signature community parade.

events.title: Hill-O-Ween at Eastern Market
events.venue: Eastern Market (225 7th St SE)
events.why: Capitol Hill's long-running Halloween street party, with merchant trick-or-treating, costumes and face painting on a closed-off block.

events.title: Día de los Muertos at the National Museum of the American Indian
events.venue: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian (4th St & Independence Ave SW)
events.why: Folk dance performances, marigold-covered ofrendas, mask-making and music inside a warm Smithsonian museum on the Mall.

events.title: SIX the Musical (Broadway Tour)
events.venue: Hippodrome Theatre (12 N Eutaw St)
events.why: The high-energy pop musical retelling the story of Henry VIII's six wives, on tour at Baltimore's historic Hippodrome.

events.title: Takoma Park Monster Bash
events.venue: Takoma Park Middle School (7611 Piney Branch Rd) to Carroll Ave
events.why: The city's annual costume parade and festival, with a DJ, games and trick-or-treating along Carroll Avenue.

events.title: Celebración Día de los Muertos at The Wharf
events.venue: The Wharf (760 Maine Ave SW)
events.why: A waterfront Day of the Dead celebration with mariachi, sugar skull decorating, face painting and an evening lantern procession.

events.title: Wheaton Halloween Eye Spy Train & Carousel
events.venue: Wheaton Regional Park (2002 Shorefield Rd)
events.why: Last day of the season for the miniature train's Halloween character hunt through the woods, plus the hand-painted carousel.

events.title: Glen Echo Park Fall Afternoon
events.venue: Glen Echo Park (7300 MacArthur Blvd)
events.why: A historic arts park with Art Deco buildings, paved paths, open lawns and a playground, free to wander.

events.title: Meadowlark Winter Walk of Lights
events.venue: Meadowlark Botanical Gardens (9750 Meadowlark Gardens Ct)
events.why: A paved half-mile garden loop through animated light displays and lakeside reflections, with s'mores fire pits along the way.

events.title: Downtown DC Holiday Market
events.time: Mon–Fri noon–8 p.m.; Sat–Sun 11 a.m.–8 p.m. (closed Nov. 26 and 30)
events.venue: 1500 block of New Hampshire Ave NW
events.why: The city's big open-air holiday market, with dozens of regional artisans, hot cider, churros and live music.

events.title: Handwork: Contemporary Craft at the Renwick Gallery
events.venue: Smithsonian American Art Museum's Renwick Gallery (1661 Pennsylvania Ave NW)
events.why: A major new craft exhibition of about 50 works arranged around the senses, including dozens of recent acquisitions.

events.title: Brookland Arts Walk Open Studios
events.venue: Brookland Arts Walk, Monroe Street Market (716 Monroe St NE)
events.why: Browse 27 working artist studios and local prints and ceramics on an easy, car-free Saturday walk.

events.title: Takoma Park Farmers Market
events.venue: Laurel Ave
events.why: A car-free street market with local produce, baked goods, warm cider and street musicians.

events.title: Garden of Lights at Brookside Gardens
events.venue: Brookside Gardens (1800 Glenallan Ave)
events.why: More than a million lights along a paved half-mile garden loop, with tickets sold only online in advance.

events.title: ZooLights at the Smithsonian's National Zoo
events.venue: Smithsonian's National Zoo (3001 Connecticut Ave NW)
events.why: DC's signature holiday light show, with glowing animal lanterns, seasonal treats and a zoo train ride.

events.title: Christmas Village in Baltimore
events.venue: West Shore Park, Inner Harbor (501 Light St)
events.price: Free entry; some areas and rides ticketed
events.why: A German-style Christmas market with dozens of wooden huts, mulled wine, bratwurst and a Ferris wheel on the Inner Harbor.

events.title: J.A.M. Christmas Vacation: Santa's Musical Spectacular Revue
events.venue: Joe's Movement Emporium (3309 Bunker Hill Rd)
events.why: A high-energy holiday song-and-dance revue mixing Christmas classics with hits from across the decades in an intimate theater.

events.title: Montgomery County Thanksgiving Parade
events.venue: Downtown Silver Spring (Ellsworth Dr & Fenton St, along Georgia Ave)
events.why: The region's only Thanksgiving parade, with giant character balloons, marching bands, floats and Santa along wide sidewalks.

events.title: Season's Greenings: National Parks and Historic Places
events.time: 10 a.m.–5 p.m. daily, closed Dec. 25; until 8 p.m. select Tue/Thu
events.venue: U.S. Botanic Garden
events.why: The holiday poinsettia show and outdoor model trains, with miniature national parks for America's 250th. Warm indoors and stroller friendly.

events.title: Enchant Christmas DC
events.venue: Nationals Park (1500 S Capitol St SE)
events.why: A giant walk-through light maze on the ballfield, with an ice-skating trail and a holiday village.

events.title: Takoma Park Flea and Art Market
events.venue: Seekers Church (276 Carroll St NW)
events.why: A Small Business Saturday edition of this monthly artisan and vintage market a short walk from the Takoma Metro.

events.title: Wegmans Wonderplace
events.venue: National Museum of American History
events.why: Indoor early-childhood gallery for ages 0–6 with play kitchens and crawl space. Pairs with the Botanic Garden.

events.title: Annapolis Grand Illumination
events.venue: Market Space, Historic Downtown
events.why: Live music, ornament making and Santa's arrival at the harborfront tree lighting. Wraps before bedtime.

events.title: 55th Annual Washington Monument Lighting
events.venue: Mount Vernon Place (699 Washington Place)
events.why: Baltimore's holiday kickoff with brass and choir performances, food and cider vendors, and fireworks over the lit monument.

events.title: National Christmas Tree & Pathway of Peace
events.venue: President's Park / The Ellipse (15th & E St NW)
events.why: Walk the Pathway of Peace past trees for every state and territory surrounding the lit National Christmas Tree.

events.title: Heurich House Christmas Markt
events.venue: Heurich House Museum, Dupont Circle
events.why: Juried all-local maker market in a historic mansion garden, with Glühwein. Four days only.

events.title: 9th Annual Mount Rainier Holiday Craft Fair
events.venue: Joe's Movement Emporium (3309 Bunker Hill Rd)
events.why: An indoor Gateway Arts District craft fair with local makers and community performers.

events.title: Alexandria Scottish Christmas Walk Parade & Holiday Boat Parade of Lights
events.time: Walk 10:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m.; boat parade 5:30 p.m.
events.venue: Old Town Alexandria
events.why: Bagpipers, tartan-clad clans and Scottish terriers parade through Old Town, followed by lighted boats on the Potomac at dusk.

events.title: The Wharf Holiday Boat Parade & Party
events.venue: The Wharf / District Pier (760 Maine Ave SW)
events.why: Dozens of decorated boats cruise the Washington Channel, with live music, kids' crafts and a fireworks finale.

events.title: Yalda Bazar: Winter Solstice
events.venue: Brookland Arts Walk
events.why: 30-plus food and art vendors, a DJ and kids' activities on a paved promenade.

events.title: 44th Annual Eastport Yacht Club Lights Parade
events.venue: Annapolis Harbor & Spa Creek
events.why: Dozens of elaborately lit boats parade through Spa Creek and the harbor, best seen from Eastport's street ends.
